title: A Tadpole Is Causing Your Hiccups
sources: Straus et al., BioEssays 2003, 'A phylogenetic hypothesis for the origin of hiccough' (gill-ventilation motor pattern, glottal closure)
Neil Shubin, Your Inner Fish, excerpt on hiccups and tadpoles (Panda's Thumb, 2008)
UCL News, 12 Nov 2019, 'Newborn baby hiccups could be key to brain development' (Whitehead et al., Clinical Neurophysiology; 13 infants; womb from nine weeks)
Smithsonian Magazine, Charles Osborne hiccuped 1922-1990, est. 430 million; Guinness World Records 2023, more than 420 million

lines.text: There's a tadpole in your throat, and it just ruined your meeting.
lines.caps: THERE'S A *TADPOLE | IN YOUR *THROAT | AND IT JUST *RUINED | YOUR *MEETING

lines.text: This is Grandpa Tadpole. Well, sort of.
A hiccup is one sharp gulp of air, then your throat slams shut. Hic!
lines.caps: A *HICCUP IS | ONE SHARP *GULP | OF *AIR | THEN YOUR *THROAT | *SLAMS SHUT | *HIC!

lines.text: Tadpoles do that exact move. They close a little gate, so water stays out of their lungs while their gills work.
lines.caps: *TADPOLES DO | THAT EXACT *MOVE | THEY *CLOSE | A LITTLE *GATE | SO *WATER | STAYS *OUT | OF THEIR *LUNGS | WHILE THEIR *GILLS | *WORK

lines.text: Scientists think we inherited that ancient wiring, and it never got the memo that you live on land.
lines.caps: *SCIENTISTS THINK | WE *INHERITED | THAT ANCIENT *WIRING | AND IT *NEVER | GOT THE *MEMO | THAT YOU LIVE | ON *LAND

lines.text: One farmer hiccuped for sixty-eight years. That's over four hundred million hics.
But here's the twist. Babies start hiccuping in the womb, at nine weeks. And one small study suggests each hic may teach a newborn's brain how to breathe.
lines.caps: BUT HERE'S THE *TWIST | *BABIES START | *HICCUPING | IN THE *WOMB | AT NINE *WEEKS | AND ONE *SMALL | STUDY *SUGGESTS | EACH HIC *MAY | *TEACH A | NEWBORN'S *BRAIN | HOW TO *BREATHE

lines.text: So next time your meeting goes silent...
